name: Fortifications of Kotor
label: Kotor Fortress
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Muo' (1 web pages); placed at OpenStreetMap 'Muo' (node/2026761099): point.
pin_note: Position set at the correction gate (2026-11-20: restored; pin on OSM W207438435 Fort of St John (name differs, no Wikidata tag)).
notes: Walls climbing the hill to the viewpoint over the bay.

text.description:
Kotor's fortifications are the long defensive walls, towers, gates and bastions that wrap around the Old Town and then climb the steep mountainside behind it. The best-known sight is the line of wall zigzagging up towards the castle of San Giovanni, at about 280 m elevation. That makes a strong shape for a phone photo: terracotta roofs and stone at the bottom, then the wall rising to a pale skyline.

The outer wall is about 4.5 km round, between 2 and 16 m thick and up to 20 m high. The hill was fortified in Illyrian times, and the Byzantines, Venetians and Austrians all added to it. Most of what you see today was built by the Venetians, who took over in 1420. The walls, together with the Old Town, have been a World Heritage Site since 1979.

For this view, use the waterfront at Muo, across the narrow inlet from the Old Town. You see the walls from sea level, with the water in front, and the stone can turn gold at sunset. It is a public street rather than part of the fortress, so you can take your time. Two other viewpoints are worth knowing about. The road towards the Fort of St Ivan gives a view over the terracotta roofs and the bay, but it lies past the paid entry at the town-wall arch, so check current access. The Gurdić Bastion shows harbour-side walls with boats.
text.geographic_location: The fortifications surround the Old Town of Kotor, at the innermost end of the Bay of Kotor, and climb the mountain of St John behind it. The Muo viewpoint is on the waterfront of the village across the inlet from the Old Town.
text.directions_text: No Underground, tram or rail stops are given for this spot. From the Old Town, go round the head of the inlet to Muo, heading north-west, and look for the Muo waterfront. The waterfront is about 1.4 km from the fortifications in a straight line. Once you are on the waterfront, face south-east towards the walls and the mountain. The phone icon on the map is at the subject itself. The Navigate buttons below take you straight there.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for the whole scene: water, Old Town and wall climbing the hill. Then try telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) to pick out the line of the wall and the castle on the ridge. Use the ultra-wide (0.5x) only if you want a lot of foreground waterfront, as it makes the walls look small and far away.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand right at the subject: the phone icon on the map marks the spot. From here you see the Old Town and the fortress walls from sea level across the narrow stretch of water. Use the waterfront edge to keep the water in the lower part of the frame.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and put the waterline on the lower grid line so the horizon stays level. Leave the top third for the wall and the mountain. If you have time, try a second viewpoint: the road towards the Fort of St Ivan gives a higher view of the roofs, the bay and the Church of Our Lady of Remedy in the foreground.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the golden stone of the wall to set focus, then drag the exposure slider down a little so the sunset light does not wash out the detail. Check that the sky and the walls both look right before you take the shot. Take a Live Photo too, as moving water or passing boats can give you a better frame. After sunset, use night mode and hold your phone still.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Sunset, when the walls turn gold. Early evening is a good time to be in place a little beforehand and take several frames as the light changes.

text.access_note: The Muo waterfront is a public street and free to stand on, but climbing the fortress itself may be ticketed or restricted, so check the official site before you go.

name: Kotor Cathedral
label: Cathedral of St Trypho
camera_source: Commons cluster (33 photos). Moved 17 m outwards on 2026-11-10 so it is 30 m from the subject's edge, as the text says.
pin_note: Position from OpenStreetMap way/165389709: the middle of the OpenStreetMap outline 'St. Tryphon Cathedral' (43 m across).

text.description:
Kotor Cathedral, dedicated to Saint Tryphon, is the seat of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Kotor, which covers the Bay of Kotor, and the building most closely linked with the town's identity. Saint Tryphon is Kotor's patron and appears on the city's coat of arms. The cathedral was consecrated on 19 June 1166, on the site of an older church from 809. It is Romanesque in style and is one of the largest and most ornate buildings in the town. It has been through a lot: it was badly damaged in the 1667 earthquake and again in the 1979 earthquake, and a long renovation was celebrated with a blessing in December 2000.

For photographs, the cathedral works well because it is a large stone building with plenty of detail. Frame the whole front for a record shot, then move in for the texture of the stonework. Inside, there are 14th-century frescoes and a carved stone ornament above the main altar telling the story of Saint Tryphon. Check the official site before you go to find out what you can visit and whether photography is allowed inside.

The phone icon on the map is close, so you will be looking up at the building. Keep your phone upright to catch the height, and use the gridlines to keep the walls from leaning. Take a few steps back or sideways to try a different angle before you move on.
text.geographic_location: Inside the walled old town of Kotor, in the historic centre of the city. It is the cathedral of Saint Tryphon, the town's patron saint.
text.directions_text: No Underground, tram or train stops are listed for Kotor, so start from the old town of Kotor. The phone icon on the map is about 30 m west of the subject. The Navigate buttons below take you straight there.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the ultra-wide (0.5x) to fit the whole building in from this close, then switch to the default lens (1x) for a more natural view. If your phone has a telephoto (2x-5x), use it for carvings and details higher up.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand about 30 m west of the subject, at the phone icon on the map, and face east. You are close, so the building will fill much of the frame.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Switch on gridlines and line the edges of the building up with the vertical lines so the walls stand straight. Hold the phone upright for the full height, or turn it sideways to include the surroundings. Try the ultra-wide for the whole front, then the default lens (1x) or telephoto for details.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the cathedral to focus, then lower the exposure slider a little if the pale stone looks washed out against the sky. Take a wide shot and a close one in case people walk through the frame.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Early morning or late afternoon usually means softer light and fewer people. If you want to see inside, check the official site for visiting arrangements before you go.

text.access_note: The cathedral is a working place of worship, so check the official site before you go for visiting arrangements and any entry rules.
claims_not_in_sources: Early morning or late afternoon usually has softer light and fewer visitors in Kotor's old town.
Pale stone can look overexposed in bright light, so lowering the exposure slider may help.
Photography inside the cathedral may be restricted, so visitors should check the official site.
The cathedral is a working place of worship with its own visiting arrangements.

name: Church of Our Lady of Remedy
label: Our Lady of Remedy
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'San Giovanni Fortress' (2 web pages); placed at our map tiles: 'San Giovanni' (pois).
pin_note: Position set at the correction gate (pin check 2026-11-18: moved onto the OSM object with the sight's Wikidata ID).
notes: Small church halfway up the fortress path.

text.description:
Perched on the slope of St John Mountain above Kotor's Old Town, the Church of Our Lady of Remedy (also called Gospa od Zdravlja, or Our Lady of Health) is a small Roman Catholic church that looks wonderful against the bay. Its pale stone stands out against the hillside, and the water, the Old Town walls and the Vrmac ridge fill the space behind it. That layered view is why it works so well on a phone.

The church was completed in 1518. Visitors can only reach it on foot, up a stairway of more than 650 steps. An early Christian basilica from the 6th century has been found beneath it, the oldest known building in Montenegro. It stood close to the main gate of the Old Town.

For a higher view, San Giovanni Fortress, further up the fortress path and above the church, looks down on the church with the bay and the town walls behind it, and it is often quieter than the church-level frame. The Road to the Fort of St Ivan is another option, showing the church in the foreground to middle distance, with the Old Town rooftops, the bay and the ridge behind.

Take the climb slowly, stop to photograph on the way up, and keep the church, the water and the ridge all in one frame.
text.geographic_location: On the slope of St John Mountain above Kotor's Old Town. The fortress path continues higher up the hill above the church.
text.directions_text: Start in Kotor's Old Town, near the main city gate. The path up the hillside is a long climb of steps, and the way in is through a small gate in the town walls. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) to show the church with the bay and ridge behind it. Switch to ultra-wide (0.5x) if you want more of the Old Town walls and the whole sweep of the bay. Use the telephoto lens (2x or more, depending on your phone) to pick out the church without the surroundings getting in the way.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand right at the subject (higher on the fortress path, above the church). The church set against the bay, the Old Town walls and the Vrmac ridge, shot from above. The Road to the Fort of St Ivan is another place to try, as it shows the church in the foreground to middle distance.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on the gridlines and put the church on one of the lower thirds, so the bay and the ridge fill the upper part of the frame. Include a stretch of the Old Town walls or rooftops to give a sense of scale. For a wider view, try panorama mode and sweep slowly from the church across to the water.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the church to set focus, then slide the exposure down a little if the sky or the water looks washed out. Hold the phone steady with both hands, as there may be a breeze higher up.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Early morning or late afternoon usually gives softer light and fewer people on the path. Bright midday sun can flatten the view and wash out the bay.

text.access_note: The church can only be reached on foot via a long stairway, and the fortress path has a small entry fee at the town-wall gate, so check the official site before you go for current fees and opening times.
claims_not_in_sources: Early morning or late afternoon usually gives softer light and fewer people on the fortress path.
Bright midday sun can flatten the view and wash out the bay.
There may be a breeze higher up the hill.

name: Sea Gate of Kotor
label: Sea Gate
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Riva' (3 web pages); placed at OpenStreetMap 'Riva' (relation/21077379): middle (195 m across).
pin_note: Position from OSM W146338061 (Sea gate): kept: no OpenStreetMap object carries this Wikidata ID.
notes: The main entrance to the walled Old Town.

text.description:
The Sea Gate is a busy waterfront entrance to Kotor's Old Town, and the view from the promenade is the classic composition of the gate. From the Riva you see the arch and the base of the Old Town walls with the mountains rising behind, and boat masts add a lively foreground. Above the arch is a carved lion of St Mark, which is a good detail to look for. It is a busy entrance for cruise passengers, so the gate can be crowded later in the day.

The composition works well on a phone because it is simple. Stand on the promenade, put the gate in the middle of the frame and let the walls and mountains fill the background. Turn on gridlines so the walls stay straight. Keep the masts at the edge of the frame so they lead the eye towards the gate rather than cutting across it. Go early if you can: the light is cleanest in the morning and there are fewer people in front of the arch.

For a second picture, walk through and shoot back from inside. The arch frames the bright bay beyond, and the carved details of the passage show up around it. If the walkway is busy, wait a moment for a gap and take a few frames.
text.geographic_location: The Sea Gate is on the waterfront edge of Kotor's Old Town, facing the Riva promenade. The best view is from the promenade just outside it.
text.directions_text: No rail or tram stops are mapped nearby, so start from the Old Town waterfront in Kotor and walk to the middle of the Riva promenade. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for the classic view of the gate. If you are close and the walls are cut off, switch to the ultra-wide (0.5x). Use 2x if your phone has it to pick out the lion above the arch.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand on Riva (middle of the waterfront promenade, roughly opposite the Sea Gate, shooting slightly north). The Sea Gate and the base of the Old Town walls against the mountains, with boat masts in the foreground.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Centre the gate with the mountains behind and let the masts sit along the bottom or side of the frame. Use the gridlines to keep the walls level. For a different angle, go through to the inside of the arch and frame the bright bay beyond it, with the carved details around the passage.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the stone of the gate to set focus, then drag the exposure slider down a little so the bright sky does not wash out the detail. Take a few frames in case people walk through.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Early morning, ideally before about 9:00 in summer, when light falls on the lion of St Mark above the arch and the entrance is quietest.

text.access_note: The Riva promenade is a public waterfront street and this view needs no climb or paid access; for anything beyond the gate, check the official site before you go.
claims_not_in_sources: The Riva promenade lies directly outside the gate, so the gate is reached by walking from the promenade into the Old Town.
The 0.5x lens helps when standing close to the walls.

name: Clock Tower of Kotor
label: Clock Tower
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Trg od Oružja' (4 web pages); placed at our map tiles: 'Pjaca od Oružja' (pois).
pin_note: Position from OSM W197926378 (The Clock Tower): kept: no OpenStreetMap object carries this Wikidata ID.
notes: 17th-century tower beside the Square of Arms.

text.description:
The Clock Tower stands in Kotor's Old Town on Trg od Oružja (Arms Square), and it is a much-photographed landmark of the Old Town. Its stone facade leans noticeably, and the clock head sits high up. Stone buildings crowd in on either side, and the mountains rise behind them. That mix of weathered stone, a clock face and a steep green backdrop makes the picture look like Kotor at a glance.

The classic angle is from the square itself, standing directly in front of the tower and looking straight at it. From there you get the detail of the facade and the clock head, with the neighbouring buildings acting as a frame and the mountains behind. A pillar of shame stands in front of the tower and can drift into the bottom of your shot. You can use it as a foreground detail or step sideways to leave it out.

The square is busy, and cruise groups make it very crowded during the day, so early morning is the best time for a clear view. Late afternoon around golden hour is also recommended. If you want a wider scene, walk over to Trg Sv. Tripuna, the neighbouring cathedral square. From there the tower sits among the cathedral facade and the old town buildings. Take a few frames at each spot, because the two views look quite different.
text.geographic_location: In the heart of Kotor's Old Town, on Trg od Oružja (Arms Square), right next to the cathedral square, Trg Sv. Tripuna.
text.directions_text: No train or bus stops are listed for this spot, so head for the Old Town of Kotor. Once inside the walls, make for Trg od Oružja, the square the tower stands on. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) to fit the whole tower with the mountains behind it. Use the telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) for the clock head and the stonework. The ultra-wide (0.5x) helps if the square is too tight to step back.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand in Trg od Oružja (standing directly in front of the tower, facing it). The tower's tilted stone facade and clock head, framed by the surrounding stone buildings and the mountain backdrop.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on the gridlines and line the tower up on one of the vertical lines, with the clock head near the upper crossing. Keep the phone level, because a tilted phone makes the already leaning facade look odd. Watch for the pillar of shame at the bottom of the frame. For a wider alternative, walk over to Trg Sv. Tripuna, where the tower sits with the cathedral facade and the old town buildings around it.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the stone facade to set focus, then drag the exposure slider down a little if the sky behind looks washed out. With the ultra-wide (0.5x), keep the tower in the middle of the frame so its edges are not stretched.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Early morning, when soft sunlight falls on the tower and the crowds are thinner. Golden hour in the late afternoon is also a good choice.

text.access_note: The square is an open public space and free to stand in.
claims_not_in_sources: The tower's facade appears to lean, as it is described as tilted.
Tilting the phone makes a leaning facade look odd, and the ultra-wide (0.5x) lens can stretch objects near the edges of the frame.
Lowering the exposure slider can help if the sky behind the tower looks washed out.

name: Square of Arms
label: Square of Arms
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Trg od Oružja' (3 web pages); placed at our map tiles: 'Pjaca od Oružja' (pois).
pin_note: Position from Wikidata Q7839643: kept: no OpenStreetMap object carries this Wikidata ID.
notes: The largest square of the Old Town.

text.description:
Trg od Oružja, or Arms Square, is the main and largest square in Kotor. The name goes back to Venetian times, when munitions were made and stored here. Today it is lined with cafés, bakeries, shops and banks.

It photographs well because everything is arranged around one clear focal point. The Clock Tower, built in the 17th century, stands across the open limestone paving. It is partly Baroque, while its northern and eastern faces are Gothic, and a reconstructed medieval pillory stands in front of it. Guides call it the square's most photographed landmark. On the way you also pass the Sea Gate, a 16th-century gateway and the biggest of the town's three, and the 17th-century Rector's Palace, now part of Hotel Cattaro. Napoleon's Theatre, turned into a theatre in 1810, is here too and now holds the hotel's reception.

The simplest classic photo is taken from near the Sea Gate end, looking across the square to the Clock Tower. The Venetian-style facades and café fronts frame it on either side. Keep the tower central and the paving in the lower part of the picture, so the open space gives the scene depth. The square is much quieter early in the day, and cruise-ship groups fill it by about 10 am in summer.
text.geographic_location: In the heart of Kotor Old Town, just inside the Sea Gate, the main entrance to the walled town. The Clock Tower stands on the square, and the Rector's Palace shores up its western side.
text.directions_text: The Sea Gate is the main entrance to Kotor Old Town, and the square lies within the Old Town. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Use the default lens (1x) for the main shot. One guide suggests avoiding the widest view because it can make the buildings look small and far away. Switch to the ultra-wide (0.5x) only if you want to include the whole square and the facades on both sides.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand in Trg od Oružja (near the Sea Gate (Vrata od Mora) end, looking across the square toward the Clock Tower). The Clock Tower standing across the open limestone paving, with the square's Venetian-style facades and cafés framing it.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and put the Clock Tower on the central vertical line, with the paving filling the bottom third. Keep the phone level so the tower and the buildings do not lean. If you want a closer shot of the clock face and the pillory, try 2x or more rather than walking into the crowd.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the tower to focus, then slide the exposure down a little if the sky is bright, so the stone keeps its detail. Take a few frames in a row, because people walk through the scene constantly.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Early morning, before about 8 am, is the quietest, with almost no tour groups. Late afternoon, roughly 5 to 7 pm, is suggested for warm light on the tower. The two guides disagree, so choose whichever suits your day.

text.access_note: The square is an open public space; the hotel and any other buildings around it may have their own access rules, so check the official site before you go.
claims_not_in_sources: Gridlines and a level phone help keep the tower and buildings from leaning.
Cafés on the square may have tables or people in the foreground of the shot.
Pointing at a bright sky can make the stonework look dark, so lowering exposure helps.

name: Church of St. Luke
label: St Luke's Church
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Crkva Svetog Luke' (2 web pages); placed at OpenStreetMap 'Crkva sv. Luke' (way/207626327): middle (17 m across); moved 5 m off buildings.
pin_note: Position from OpenStreetMap way/207626327: the middle of the OpenStreetMap outline 'Church of Saint Luke' (17 m across).
notes: Small 12th-century church on St Luke's Square.

text.description: The Church of St. Luke is a small stone church in Kotor's Old Town, and it is easy to walk past. That is part of its appeal: it is tiny, so one frame can hold the whole building along with the small square around it. It dates to 1195, in the reign of Stefan Nemanja. It belongs to the Serbian Orthodox Church and mixes Byzantine and Gothic architecture. Inside, the iconostasis icons were painted in the 17th century by Dimitrije Daskal. For the west façade, with its dated inscription and Romanesque window, you walk up to the church. This close view is a quieter, more architectural picture than the wide square. For the wider scene, step back into Trg Svetog Luke (St Luke's Square). There the little church fronts the square, and the domes of the much larger St Nicholas church rise behind it to the right. Because the church is so small and the square is tight, the ultra-wide lens (0.5x) is a real help. Keep your phone level, switch on the gridlines so the walls stay straight, and take a few frames at different distances.
text.geographic_location: The church stands on Trg Svetog Luke (St Luke's Square), a small square in Kotor's Old Town, a short walk north-east of St Tryphon's Cathedral. It sits close to the much larger St Nicholas church.
text.directions_text: No Underground, tram or similar stop is listed for this spot, so head for Kotor Old Town. Make for St Tryphon's Cathedral, then walk a short way north-east to St Luke's Square. On older maps the square may appear as Trg Bratstva i jedinstva. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Use the ultra-wide (0.5x) to fit the church and the square together. Use the default lens (1x) for the west façade. Use the telephoto (2x or more, depending on your phone) for the Romanesque window and the inscription.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand right at the subject (the west façade, where the dated inscription is). A close view of the church's west façade and its Romanesque window, for a more architectural frame away from the square's wider scene.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on the gridlines and line the church's vertical edges up with them so the walls do not lean. Take one frame of the whole façade, then move closer and zoom in on the window and the inscription. For the wider alternative, take a step back into Trg Svetog Luke and shoot the little church with the domes of St Nicholas rising behind it on the right.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the stone wall to focus, then drag the exposure slider down a touch if the sky is washing out. If you shoot at 0.5x, keep the church away from the edges of the frame, because buildings can stretch there.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: No fixed time is needed. A softer, lower sun usually flatters old stone, but the square is small and shaded in places, so check how the light falls when you arrive.

text.access_note: The church is a place of worship in a public square; no opening details are given here, so check the official site before you go, and dress modestly if you plan to go inside.
